newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt detains 45 suspected Moslem militants.
newsitem.headline: Egypt detains 45 suspected Moslem militants.

text.p: Egyptian police on Saturday detained for questioning 45 suspected members of a Moslem militant group on charges of plotting to kill high-ranking officials, sources at the prosecutor's office said.

They said the detainees were members of the Qutbiyeen group, a spin-off of the illegal and influential Moslem Brotherhood. The Qutbiyeen take their name from one of the Brotherhood's key members, Sayed Qutb, who was executed by the state in the 1960s.

The group believes that the structure of Egyptian society contradicts Islamic principles and that Islamic sharia law is the only true way to govern. Unlike the Brotherhood, which believes in changing the government by political means, the sources said the Qutbiyeen resort to violence.
More than 1,000 people have been killed and hundreds wounded since Moslem militant groups began fighting the government in 1992 to set up a strict Islamic state.
The police captured the group, and seven of their leaders, in several districts of Cairo, the sources said. The prosecutor will hold them in custody for 15 days pending investigations, they added.
